assessments.reasoning: The pinned SPDX template/MIT.template.txt URL supplied the complete matcher. Its verified size and digest matched the claim. Its directives and two terminal LF bytes participated in the successful template-field comparison. Substituting the same intact body for plain text failed.

The complete, digest-verified MIT detail object at the same SPDX commit supplied both named fields. JSON decoding recovered the template delimiters and literal pattern backslashes. Switching the comparison field from standardLicenseTemplate to licenseText changed the result from equal to unequal for the same candidate.

The digest-verified text/MIT.txt from the same SPDX commit provided the independent plain-file comparator. It matched decoded licenseText throughout. Comparing the entire substitute template with this file failed at the first byte, and their lengths also differed.

challenge.method: Used the entire unmodified template as a candidate install text and tested it against both decoded MIT fields and the complete plain file.
challenge.results: The candidate passed the template-field comparison and failed both plain-text comparisons. The discrepancy begins at byte offset 0, where the template has 0x3c and the plain file has 0x4d. A check against the template field alone would accept this substitution. That result supports the claimed distinction.

limitations: The result concerns the exact pinned template, plain file and named fields. The substitution challenge was an in-memory comparison. It establishes no actual installation, formal SPDX matching outcome or redistribution authority.
reasoning: The prescribed comparison returned true for both template equality with decoded standardLicenseTemplate and template inequality with text/MIT.txt. The common template value encodes to 1,958 UTF-8 bytes with recomputed SHA-256 9b91e12dfe57d42e91ea96d2acb7624040bffc54182bd164d39d0fae33e77794. Its optional-section and variable directives are present in the compared bytes.

reproduction.reason: The execution directly compared the complete acquired source texts. Its native tool result matched an independent byte-level replay without normalization.
